facts.fact: Elven formal dress for the Convocation: greens.
Elves tie knowledge to the hand: rangers learn stones by palm from girlhood; magisters do not.
Rangers clean their blades and arrows; mucking stalls is the punishment for sloppy rangers.
Thalassian horses are fine-boned; Farstrider horses are long-legged. Elves bred speed into horses.
Rangers speak Thalassian to horses (Neral). Rangers address a human noble as 'Lady Proudmoore' / 'My lady'.

Human oath: 'Light' ('Oh, Light', 'Light help her'). Lordaeron farms keep a little wooden Light shrine with a candle on the gatepost; a rowan by the gate. A Lordaeron farmwife banks her fire at dawn; farm families keep a cart for market; people do not go out in the wind without a coat.
Human homespun metaphors: dowsing with a hazel fork; sailors know weather by gulls going inland.

Dalaran customs: apprentices work at the Violet Citadel under a porter's watch and a quartermaster's eye; the Kirin Tor have a 'long grace' before sessions. Antonidas's drill: clear the head and listen again.

Human road blessings in Lordaeron (per Sylvanas): 'Light keep you', 'Safe road', or nothing; a blessing by the stars ('May the stars keep your road') is not a Lordaeron phrase she recognises ('some hill saying'). Humans nail a horseshoe over the lintel with the points down 'when they wanted their luck to pour out over whoever walked in under it'.

Millhaven domestic details: shaving glass held to a dead mouth to test for breath; box beds; loft with straw pallets; porridge and bread, hard loaf and cheese on the table; hams kept behind the chimney breast; turnips and apples in cellars; a darned stocking with a different wool; a carved wooden toy horse with a short leg; wooden clogs worn in autumn mud; drovers bring cattle to hill grazing in spring and down in autumn; a drover holds a gate with a rope loop over the post.

Elven body-language of respect and cruelty-by-compression: Sylvanas thinks of the Convocation as 'the magister's nephew with his figures'; humans in her narration are 'a human brat' (sneer), 'human country', 'a human mage's read'.
Neral's idiom with horses: 'stand now, stand, you great fool', in Thalassian; she narrates the horse's character to a frightened child.

Village life in the sick village: a market lane with eggs, salt herring and geese; bread smoke from the bakehouse; a horseshoe nailed over the lintel with its points down and a stool with a cup on the step left for someone who will not come out; shutters barred in the day on sick houses; a Light chapel with bell-cote and no bell; sick tended in the chapel with benches carried out; willow bark, vinegar cloths, warmth and bleeding as remedies; goose grease on cracked hands; a medic who pulls teeth, sets bones and delivers babies; tooth-pulling at Midsummer; sops (bread in milk) for the toothless; oatcake on a griddle; bread and dripping; porridge before milking; bread and cheese in the field at noon bought in for hands; Mother Haw's 'shop bread is chalk'; a cage by the pound for drunks; a harvest supper at the captain's table; cockcrow as the baker's clock.
Locals call a visiting noble 'my lady' and a mage 'miss'; a captain who writes names in a ledger says each word aloud as he writes it and asks for spellings.

Kul Tiran naval culture in Jaina's references: a bosun taught her a bowline at eight (for a bet); sheet bend, clove hitch, the gunners' breeching-rope knot; gunners' swearing; Boralus cathedral with a reliquary carried down the aisle by a priest; a nurse who checked a fever with her cheek.
Farstrider teaching custom: one-handed bandage knots, left then right, in the first year; a knot is set with the teeth.

Chapter 7: Andorhal custom and texture: Lammas and midsummer mark the supplier changes; the Wheatsheaf is the loaders' tavern; a lamplighter boy with a pole at dusk; the Exchange bell rules the day; dyers hang cloth on tenter frames; a woman sings a child the same flat line. Havel greets elves correctly ('Ranger-General') unprompted; locals say 'my lady' to Jaina.
